title: firewalld and iptables
subtitle: Zones, services, panic, NAT, forwarding — flip for meaning and notes

cards.meaning: Dynamically managed firewall using zones of trust for networks/interfaces
cards.notes: Supports IPv4/IPv6, bridges, IP sets. Runtime = now; permanent = XML on disk. Default on RHEL.

cards.meaning: Runtime changes apply now; --permanent writes disk; --reload loads disk → runtime
cards.notes: Permanent alone does not change live rules until reload. Runtime-only vanishes on reload.

cards.meaning: iptables service rebuilds all rules from a file; firewalld applies only diffs
cards.notes: Full rebuild can drop connections. firewalld keeps sessions up. Kernel still uses netfilter.

cards.meaning: Stock defaults vs your overrides (zones, services)
cards.notes: On RHEL, /etc/sysconfig/iptables often does not exist — normal when firewalld is default.

cards.meaning: Lowest trust — all incoming dropped with no reply; outbound allowed
cards.notes: Remote side times out (silence), not a rejection. Contrast with block.

cards.meaning: Incoming rejected with ICMP host/adm prohibited
cards.notes: Client is told “no” instead of hanging. Similar to drop but with a reply.

cards.meaning: Untrusted networks; allow only selected incoming services
cards.example: Often default zone; allow ssh/http case by case
cards.notes: Internet / café Wi‑Fi mindset — do not trust other computers.

cards.meaning: Gateway pair — WAN with masquerade; LAN with more services
cards.example: external = toward internet; internal = private LAN
cards.notes: external hides RFC1918 behind the firewall’s public IP. internal trusts LAN more.

cards.meaning: dmz = isolated hosts, limited in; trusted = trust everyone (rare)
cards.example: Public web server in DMZ; trusted for lab only
cards.notes: work/home are fairly open office/home LANs. trusted = almost no filtering.

cards.meaning: List named services you can allow (ssh, http, ftp, …)
cards.notes: Named services wrap port + protocol (+ helpers) so you allow ftp instead of 21/tcp by hand.

cards.meaning: Show ports/modules for a named service
cards.notes: ftp → ports 21/tcp and module nf_conntrack_ftp for related data ports.

cards.meaning: Emergency: drop all packets; then leave panic mode
cards.notes: Not a zone — global nuclear switch. Can lock you out of SSH; use console for --panic-off if needed.

cards.meaning: NAT: hide internal IPs; outbound source becomes the firewall’s IP
cards.notes: Masquerade on external, not internal. Pair with --remove- / --query-masquerade.
--permanent writes XML; --reload copies permanent into runtime.

cards.meaning: DNAT: send inbound traffic for a port to another port (or toaddr)
cards.notes: Requires masquerading first — classic RHCE trap. Permanent needs --permanent then --reload.

cards.meaning: Trust level bound to an interface (or source) for how incoming traffic is handled
cards.notes: Memory hook: how much do I trust this NIC / network? Services, NAT, and forwards hang off the zone.
